questions.question: Pick the true sentence.
questions.explain: 8 is bigger than 5, so 8 > 5 is true. The wide side of the symbol always faces the bigger number.

questions.question: Maya has 14 stickers. Ben has 9 stickers. Pick the true sentence.
questions.explain: Maya has more stickers, so 14 is greater than 9. The wide end of > always faces the bigger number.

questions.question: Tom has 6 red apples and 4 green apples. Jo has 10 apples. Pick the true sentence.
questions.explain: Tom has 6 + 4, which is 10. Jo also has 10. Since both sides are the same, use the = sign.

questions.question: Ria walks 9 blocks and then 2 more. Kip walks 5 blocks and then 8 more. Pick the true sentence.
questions.explain: Ria walks 9 + 2 = 11 blocks. Kip walks 5 + 8 = 13 blocks. Since 11 is less than 13, we write 11 < 13. Do not just compare 9 and 5!

questions.question: Zoe has 20 shells. She gives 7 away and finds 5 more, so she has 18. Her friend has 13. Pick the true sentence.
questions.explain: Zoe has 18 shells and her friend has 13. Since 18 is bigger than 13, we write 18 > 13. The wide side of the symbol always faces the bigger number.

questions.question: Ben has 4 red marbles and 6 blue marbles. Mia has 9 marbles and 1 more. Pick the true sentence.
questions.explain: Ben has 4 + 6, which is 10. Mia has 9 + 1, which is also 10. Since both have the same number, use the = sign. Do not just compare 4 and 9!

questions.question: Which number sentence is true?
questions.explain: 58 has 5 tens and 85 has 8 tens, so 58 is the smaller number. The small point of the < sign always points at the smaller number.

questions.question: Leo picked 36 blueberries. Sara picked 30 blueberries. Which sentence is true?
questions.explain: 36 is more than 30, so we write 36 > 30. The open, wide end of the sign always faces the bigger number.

questions.question: Jade has 15 stickers and gives 6 to her brother. Ravi has 4 stickers and gets 7 more. Which sentence is true?
questions.explain: Jade has 15 - 6 = 9 left and Ravi has 4 + 7 = 11, so 9 is less than 11. Starting with a big number like 15 does not mean that side ends up bigger.

questions.question: At the beach Nina found 12 shells and 8 rocks. Owen found 16 shells and 4 rocks. Which sentence is true?
questions.explain: Nina has 12 + 8 = 20 and Owen has 16 + 4 = 20, so both sides match and we use =. Comparing only 12 and 16 would trick you here.

questions.question: Kim worked out 9 + 5 and 12 + 1. She wrote 9 + 5 < 12 + 1. What went wrong?
options: She added 9 + 5 and got 13 by mistake.
She read the < sign the wrong way round.
She compared 5 and 1, not the totals.
She compared 9 and 12, not the totals.
questions.explain: 9 + 5 makes 14 and 12 + 1 makes 13, so the true sentence is 9 + 5 > 12 + 1. Add up both sides before you choose the sign.

questions.question: Ty had $25 and spent $9. Ana had $30 and spent $16. Which sentence is true?
questions.explain: Ty has 25 - 9 = 16 left and Ana has 30 - 16 = 14 left, so Ty has more. Ana started with more money, but you must work out each side before comparing.

questions.question: Compare 45 and 54. Which sentence is right?
questions.explain: 54 has 5 tens and 45 has 4 tens, so 45 is the smaller number. The small point of the sign always faces the smaller number, so 45 < 54.

questions.question: Work out both sides first. Which sentence is right?
questions.explain: Add each side: 7 + 8 is 15 and 9 + 5 is 14. 15 is more, so the sign opens toward 7 + 8. Looking only at 7 and 9 gives the wrong sign.

questions.question: Which sign belongs in the box? 30 + 8 □ 28 + 10
questions.explain: 30 + 8 is 38 and 28 + 10 is 38 as well. Both sides are the same amount, so the sign is =. Choosing from 30 and 28 alone is the common trap.

questions.question: Is 40 + 9 smaller or bigger than 52? Choose the right sentence.
questions.explain: First add: 40 + 9 is 49, and 49 comes before 52 when you count. The sign opens toward the bigger side, so 40 + 9 < 52.

questions.question: Jun marks 47 and 74 on a number line. The 47 sits to the left of 74. Which sentence is right?
questions.explain: On a number line the numbers get bigger as you move right. 47 is on the left, so it is less: 47 < 74.

questions.question: At the school fair Priya wins 12 tickets and then 9 more. Sam wins 15 tickets and then 5 more. Which sentence is right?
questions.explain: Priya has 12 + 9 = 21 and Sam has 15 + 5 = 20. 21 is more, so the sign opens toward Priya, even though 12 is less than 15.

questions.question: Devi wants to know if 24 + 8 is more than 30. What should she do first?
options: Compare 24 and 30, then pick a sign.
Point the open end at the small side.
Look at 24 only, since it is first.
questions.explain: Always work out the side with the plus first: 24 + 8 is 32. Then compare 32 with 30. Comparing only 24 with 30 leads to the wrong sign.

questions.question: Rosa picks 35 raspberries before lunch and 15 after lunch. Her basket holds 50 berries. Which sentence is right?
questions.explain: 35 + 15 makes 50, exactly what the basket holds. When both sides are the same amount, the sign is =, not > or <.
